newsitem.title: UK: Ldn platinum, palladium ease from recent extremes.
newsitem.headline: Ldn platinum, palladium ease from recent extremes.

text.p: Tension in the high-strung platinum and palladium markets eased slightly on Tuesday after fresh news from Russia suggested long-delayed exports may soon be resumed.
"Hopefully last Thursday and Friday was the peak of the panic," a London based dealer said.
Both platinum and palladium were seeing a bit of selling from dealers who bought material on the way up, he added.
Platinum was toying with the $450 support level, having sunk nearly $20 from Monday's close.
It was last quoted at $446.00/451.00 an ounce.
Prices last week had soared to as high as $500, a critical resistance level which would be difficult to surmount, technical analysts said.
Similarly palladium prices, which leapt to 17-year highs last week amid extreme supply tightness, were also easier.
The last quote of $203.00/$208.00 an ounce was down $18.00 from Monday's finish.

The market was breathing slightly easier following comments early in the day from a Russian Finance ministry expert, who said the state export agency Almazjuvelirexport should this week receive a licence for export.
Receipt of a licence is a key step in resuming exports of PGMs to key importer Japan. Russia is the world's biggest producer of palladium and second largest of platinum.
"With the export licences due to be signed I would expect Russian shipments will start quite soon," the dealer said.
"Meanwhile dealers are making a conscious effort to tidy up the spot prices," he said, for instance by giving more latitude on delivery times.
Platinum was even seeing some lending, with one month rates eased to 40-50 percent, compared to 80 percent on Monday and highs of over 100 percent last week, he said.

A smidgen of spot selling -- but no lending -- featured in the palladium market, dealers said. Last week dealers stopped quoting forward prices and lease rates after palladium's overnight lease rates rocketed to over 200 percent.
Gold and silver continued to be only marginally affected by the wide movements of the PGMs.
The price of gold was fixed just softer at $343.75 versus $344.00 in the morning, and appeared reluctant to be dislodged in a narrow prices range between $341 and $347.
Silver at $4.78/4.80 was four cents off from Monday's close.
